title: Soraya's Demands
notebook: Soraya's coalition wants an unrestricted right to strike written into the constitution.
Also healthcare, education and housing in the bill of rights, limited land reform, five percent threshold.
Maric: the business class will revolt. The workers will not forget which side I stand on.

narrative.text: Soraya Khaled receives you in the Workers' Unity Hall — a converted textile factory whose walls still carry the stains of decades of labor. Photographs of past strikes line the hallway. The air smells of coal dust and determination.

Soraya asked me to speak for the coalition. She trusts me. Here is what we need, Chancellor: the right to strike must be in the constitution — unrestricted, the way the 1897 revolutionaries demanded. Social and economic rights in the bill of rights — healthcare, education, housing. Land reform — the limited kind is fine, we are not asking for revolution. And the electoral threshold at five percent or lower. The workers will never have a voice if the threshold locks out every party that represents them.
I know what you are thinking: the business class will revolt. They will. But they were never going to support you anyway. The workers will. The question is which side of history you stand on.

monologue: A converted textile factory. The stains are still on the walls. Marić is speaking for Soraya, which means Soraya has chosen not to be in the room — a strategic absence. The demands are what I expected: strike right, social rights, land reform, five percent threshold. The question is not whether I support them. The question is whether supporting all of them loses me the Halvekist votes I need to pass anything at all. Power is the ability to choose which promises to keep.

choices.text: "You will have your strike right, Gregor. Social rights in the bill of rights. Five percent threshold. The land reform — limited, as you said. I cannot give you everything. But I can give you enough to change lives."

reactions.text: He leans back in his chair. Not relaxation — release. He has been holding something tight all meeting. Strike right. Social rights. Five percent. He nods. The workers will remember this.

choices.text: "The strike right — yes. Social rights — yes. But the threshold stays at ten percent, Gregor. I need the Halvekists' support to pass this constitution. I cannot give you everything without losing everything."

reactions.text: He looks at you for a long moment. The threshold stays at ten percent. He writes it down in his block-letter script. The silence is the sound of Gregor Maric accepting less than he asked for and filing the remainder for later.
